analysis: All supplied changes are test-only. In EngineV2BridgeTests.swift the changed range is head 807-839, which the supplied head excerpts (units 11-13 cover lines 1862-3160) do not display, and the patch excerpt is the only visible view of it. In MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngineTests.swift the change is head 625-635, a new test for ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope. The tests cover three things. First, GPT-OSS client stop strings are scoped to the Harmony final channel, with opener '<|channel|>final', openerEnd '<|message|>' and closers '<|end|>', '<|return|>', '<|call|>', '<|start|>'. Second, a stop string appearing in the analysis channel does not trigger a stop. Third, the scope is plumbed through EngineV2Translation.cbv2Request into CBv2Request.stopStringScope. The visible head excerpts also contain existing tests for the shared KV budget, SSD prefix-cache receipts and the paged KV backend. I found no new attack surface or regression in the visible lines: nothing touches the TB-002 wire contract, the encrypted SSD cache (T-041), attestation or authorization (TB-011), or the fan helper. The production implementation (ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope, EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence scoping, translation) is not in this batch. The integration pass should check, in that code, that scoped stop matching is bounded in cost and memory, that a client stop string cannot cut off analysis-channel output so as to bypass the scoping, and that stop evaluation still fails closed and does not leak plaintext. This is a correctness and availability concern, not a confirmed issue. Because the changed head lines 807-839 are not displayed in full, deeper review is warranted for the production code only.
